seo.metaTitle: Text to PNG - Free Image From Text Generator, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Turn text into a PNG sized to fit the label plus padding: font, size, bold, color, background. Free, no upload, no signup, made in your browser.
seo.longDescription: Text to PNG renders a label as a picture rather than text on a web page — what you need when the words have to survive being copied into a slide, a design tool or an email where your font is not installed. The browser's own text engine measures your string, and the canvas is sized to fit the text plus the padding you set, so the result is cropped tight to the label rather than a fixed frame with empty space around it. It is drawn on your device: no upload, no source file.
facts: Drawn entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Font size from 8 to 300 px; canvas width follows the measured text.
Single line only — no wrapping; long sentences give a very wide image.
Background Opacity 0 keeps the padding fully transparent.
The glyphs come from your system's fonts, so the export looks like your machine.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: No upload needed - the image is drawn from the text you type.
Type your label into the Text field.
Set the Text style: font family, size from 8 to 300 pixels, bold and color.
Set the background Opacity and Background color; opacity 0 leaves the image transparent.
Set the Padding from 0 to 200 pixels to add space around the label.
Download the image as PNG, JPG, WebP or BMP from the Download button.

faq.q: Does my text wrap onto several lines?
faq.a: No. The canvas is sized to fit one line of text plus the padding, so a long sentence gives you a very wide, short image. If you need text laid over a picture and wrapped, use the add text tool on this site instead.

faq.q: Why does the result look different on another computer?
faq.a: Because it is rendered with the fonts installed on this device. A machine without the font you chose substitutes its own, and the measured width changes with it. Export at the size and style you actually need and check the result where it will be used.

faq.q: Can I get a transparent background?
faq.a: Set Opacity to 0 and leave the background color alone. The padding area then stays fully transparent, which keeps the PNG and WebP formats clean; saving as JPG flattens those areas to the background color instead.

faq.q: How is the image size decided?
faq.a: The width is the measured text width plus twice the padding, and the height is the font size times a fixed line height plus twice the padding. There is no separate width control - it follows the text.
